items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: He and Marge were such jolly people when you didn't have to work with them

ctx.x: The period between the 15th of December and the 15th of January is a difficult one to organize concerts, so Lily had asked the musicians if they would agree to work in a cabaret during that period, at a different price ofcourse; the tour could start again inthe second part of January. We had received an offer for the band to work at the "Chikito" in Bern, Switzerland. Everybody had agreed. We told the musicians that the club would be closed the 25th of December, and the 1st of January, and therefore, we would not…

But about two weeks after we were on tour, Zutty went into his act which I was afraid he would do, when Lily wrote to me in Germany and told me that she had engaged him for the tour. I knew he had a reputation for being moody and difficult to work with. He would be at times very unpleasant. It was a pity, because he and Marge were such jolly people when you didn't have to work with them, started to be real drags, staying for themselves, refusing friendly advances. They had an old dog named "Bring Down" travelling…

Zutty couldn't stand the pianist, and every night was growling about...that sh...pianist. He would slow down the tempo terribly, and if I said something, try to put the blame on Randy. He was making me feel miserable, and nobody was happy about that situation except Randy and Bank who didn't care and were close buddies. Those two were always up to some foolishness.
